# Gramps Connect Stories A portable, versioned file format for family-history **stories** (slides with text, dates, places on a map, and photos), plus the TypeScript package that reads, writes and validates them. A story is one `.story.zip`: a `story.json` and the media it uses. It needs no database, server or account to open, so any program can write one and any viewer can present it. [Gramps Connect](https://github.com/dsblank/gramps-connect) writes them and presents them with this package's player. - **Open a story:** the Gramps Connect Story Viewer at **https://dsblank.github.io/gramps-connect-stories/**. Pick or drop a `.story.zip`, or link to one with `?src=`; `#s3` opens a slide. Everything happens in the browser: an opened story is never uploaded. - **Change a story, or make one:** the Story Editor, at **https://dsblank.github.io/gramps-connect-stories/edit.html** (or **Edit** on an open story in the viewer). Titles, dates, text, photos, places, shapes and old maps on the map, and the order of slides; it saves a new `.story.zip`, back into the opened file in Chrome and Edge. Also entirely in the browser, except a place search on Wikidata when you ask for one. - **Put a story on a web page:** the [``](#on-any-web-page-gramps-connect-story) element. - **Format specification:** [`spec/1.0/README.md`](spec/1.0/README.md) - **JSON Schema:** [`spec/1.0/story.schema.json`](spec/1.0/story.schema.json) - **Examples:** [`examples/`](examples/) ## On any web page: `` One script tag, no build step: ```html ``` | Attribute | | |---|---| | `src` | URL of a `.story.zip`. On another site, that site has to allow it (CORS). | | `slide` | Slide to open on: an index, or a slide id like `s3`. | | `theme` | `light`, `dark`, or `auto` (the default: the viewer's setting). | It's 480px tall unless the page's CSS says otherwise (`gramps-connect-story { height: 70vh }`), and draws into a shadow root, so the page's styles and the story's don't mix. Arrow keys move between slides once a story has focus, so several can share a page. `embed.js` includes React and maplibre; the map's worker loads from beside it (from a CDN through a `blob:` URL, so a page whose Content-Security-Policy sets `worker-src` has to allow `blob:`). ## The package: `@gramps-connect/story` ```sh npm install @gramps-connect/story ``` ```ts import { readStoryZip, writeStoryZip, validate, optimizeImage, mediaBlob } from "@gramps-connect/story"; // Open a story (a File, Blob, ArrayBuffer or Uint8Array). const story = await readStoryZip(file); story.doc.title; // story.json, upgraded to the current format const url = URL.createObjectURL(mediaBlob(story, "m1")!); // Write one. Throws StoryValidationError rather than producing an invalid story. const photo = await optimizeImage(originalBlob); // 1600px WebP, EXIF/GPS removed const zip = await writeStoryZip( { title: "The Story of Anna Keller", slides: [{ id: "s0", title: "The Story of Anna Keller", media: [{ ref: "m1" }] }], media: { m1: { src: `media/m1.${photo.ext}`, mime: photo.mime, width: photo.width, height: photo.height } }, }, new Map([[`media/m1.${photo.ext}`, photo.blob]]), ); ``` | Export | What it does | |---|---| | `readStoryZip(input, limits?)` | Opens a `.story.zip`: finds `story.json`, upgrades older format versions, validates against the files present. Throws `StoryFormatError` with a `code` (`not-a-zip`, `no-story-json`, `bad-json`, `not-a-story`, `bad-version`, `newer-version`, `too-large`, `invalid`). | | `writeStoryZip(doc, files)` | Builds a `.story.zip`, filling in `format`/`version`. Photos are stored, not recompressed. | | `validate(doc, files?)` | Schema plus cross-reference checks; returns `{valid, errors, warnings}` with JSON Pointer paths. | | `upgradeStory(raw)` | Checks `format`/`version` and upgrades an older major version. | | `optimizeImage(blob, options?)` | Browser only. Resizes (1600px photos, 2048px map overlays), applies EXIF rotation, re-encodes to WebP (PNG for transparent overlays), and drops all metadata. | | `mediaBlob(story, key)` | A media file as a typed `Blob`. | | `FORMAT_VERSION`, `SUPPORTED_FORMAT_MAJORS` | The format version written, and every major version that can be read. | `validate()` runs a validator compiled ahead of time from the schema (`src/generated/`), so it works under a strict Content-Security-Policy. ## The player: `@gramps-connect/story/player` A React component that presents a story: one slide at a time over a full-bleed map when any slide has a place (with the place's shapes, historical map overlays shown in their own era, and Auto / Standard / Historical basemaps from OpenFreeMap and OpenHistoricalMap), or as plain cards when none does, with a timeline strip when two or more slides are dated. ```tsx import * as maplibregl from "maplibre-gl"; import { StoryPlayer } from "@gramps-connect/story/player"; // Tell maplibre where your bundler serves its worker (maplibre-gl 5+ // ships it as dist/maplibre-gl-worker.mjs + dist/maplibre-gl-shared.mjs, // which must sit side by side). Without this the map draws nothing. maplibregl.setWorkerUrl("/maplibre-gl-worker.mjs"); const story = await readStoryZip(file); const urls = new Map(); const resolveMedia = async (key: string) => { if (!urls.has(key)) urls.set(key, URL.createObjectURL(mediaBlob(story, key)!)); return urls.get(key)!; };
{}} />
``` It fills its container. Props: | Prop | | |---|---| | `story` | The story document (`StoryDoc`). | | `resolveMedia(key, item)` | A URL for a media key, or null. The host owns these URLs, and revoking them. | | `dark`, `colors` | Light/dark defaults, and any colors to override (`surface`, `text`, `muted`, `border`, `mark`, `panel`). | | `strings` | The player's own words (`previous`, `next`, `close`, map-mode labels). By default, built-in English, German, Spanish, French or Dutch, by the story's language and then the browser's. | | `onClose` | Shows a close button. | | `keyboard` | Arrow keys change slides: `true` (default) anywhere on the page, `"focus"` only while the player has focus, `false` never. Swiping on a slide always works. | | `onSlideChange(index)` | Called whenever the slide changes. | | `initialSlide` | The slide to open on. | | `brand` | Shown before the title, e.g. `ViewerBrand`. | | `actions` | Your own buttons, at the right of the title bar. | | `renderMapModeControl` | Replaces the built-in map-mode control with your own, given the same props. | Peer dependencies: `react`, `react-dom` and `maplibre-gl` (5 or later), needed only by the player. With TypeScript 6 or later, add `"geojson"` to `compilerOptions.types`: maplibre's own declarations use its global `GeoJSON` namespace. ## The editor: `@gramps-connect/story/editor` A React component that edits a story: the slides on the left (drag to reorder), the selected slide's title, date, text, place and photos in the middle, and the player on the right showing it as it changes, with undo and redo and the format's validation as you go. Photos are added by picking, dropping or pasting, prepared in the browser (`optimizeImage`: resized, metadata left behind) and stored once however many slides show them. It edits the story; opening and saving files is up to you (the Story Editor page uses the File System Access API where there is one, a download where not). ```tsx import "@mantine/core/styles.css"; import { MantineProvider } from "@mantine/core"; import { StoryEditor, pruneMedia } from "@gramps-connect/story/editor"; import { writeStoryZip } from "@gramps-connect/story"; let latest = { doc: story.doc, files: story.files }; (latest = { doc, files })} /> // Saving: leave out media nothing uses any more, then zip. const saved = pruneMedia(latest.doc, latest.files); const zip = await writeStoryZip(saved.doc, saved.files); ``` A date is typed as readers should see it ("about 1850", "um 1850"), and its precise form (EDTF, for the timeline and historical maps) is worked out from it, in the story's language, by [`@gramps-connect/gramps-date`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@gramps-connect/gramps-date): Gramps' own date parser, in all of Gramps' languages. Pass `parseDateText` to use another. Fields the editor doesn't know are kept as they are, so opening and saving a story never loses anything. A place is a name and a point: click the map or drag the pin, type the coordinates, or pick one of the story's other places to use the very same one (its shape and map overlays too). **Find on Wikidata** looks the name up and puts the pin there; it's the only thing the editor sends anywhere, the name only, and only when clicked. Pass `placeSearch` to use another service, or `placeSearch={null}` to leave it out. **Edit map** opens the place's map full screen: draw shapes (points, lines, areas) or import them from a KML, GPX or GeoJSON file, and lay scans of old maps over it (stored at up to 2048px, PNG when they have transparency), moving, resizing, rotating or dragging their corners to line them up, with the years each one shows. The map editor itself is `MapEditor`, which Gramps Connect's own map overlay editor uses too; the plain functions behind it (map files, the shape model, overlay geometry) are `@gramps-connect/story/map-edit`. The editor also needs `terra-draw` and `terra-draw-maplibre-gl-adapter` (optional peer dependencies). The editor is built with [Mantine](https://mantine.dev) 8 (optional peer dependencies `@mantine/core` and `@mantine/hooks`, needed only by the editor): wrap it in a `MantineProvider` and load Mantine's stylesheet. The pieces it's made of (`SlideList`, `StoryTextField`, `DateField`, `PlaceField`, `PhotosField`, `MapEditor`, `PlaceMapDialog`) and its editing functions (`addSlide`, `moveSlide`, `updateSlide`, `addImage`, undo history (`History`, for any document), ...) are exported too. ## Writing stories from Python: `python/gramps_connect_story.py` One file, standard library only, for programs that aren't JavaScript. Copy it into your project. It's **GPL-2.0-or-later** (unlike the rest of this repo), so GPL programs such as Gramps addons can include it. ```python from gramps_connect_story import Story story = Story("The Story of Josef Meyer", language="en") story.add_slide( title="Birth", text="Josef was born *about* 1850.", date={"text": "about 1850", "edtf": "1850~", "sortYear": 1850}, place={"name": "Zürich", "lat": 47.37, "lon": 8.54}, photo="portrait.jpg", ) story.write("josef.story.zip") ``` With [Pillow](https://python-pillow.org/) installed, photos are sized for viewing (1600px, WebP) with their metadata removed; without it they're stored as they are. `write()` checks what a writer can get wrong (ids, references, coordinates) and the tests check the output against this package's own reader (`npm run test:python`). The Gramps desktop addon **Export Story** (Tools → Utilities, in `gramps-project/addons-source`) ships a copy of this file; keep the two identical. ## Development ```sh npm install npm test # Node tests (examples, versioning, validation, zip handling) npm run test:browser # in headless Google Chrome: optimizeImage(), the player, # the embed (cross-origin), the viewer site and the editor npm run test:pack # what npm would get, installed into an empty project npm run test:python # the Python writer, and its output read by this package npm run typecheck npm run generate # after editing spec/*/story.schema.json npm run build # dist/ (what npm users get) npm run build:site # site-dist/ (the viewer and the editor) ``` Gramps Connect includes this repo as a git submodule and compiles `src/` directly (the `source` export condition), so it never needs `dist/`. ## Releasing The viewer site redeploys from `main` on every push (`.github/workflows/pages.yml`). An npm release is a version tag: ```sh # bump "version" in package.json, commit and push, then: git tag v0.2.0 && git push origin v0.2.0 ``` `.github/workflows/release.yml` then runs every test and publishes with provenance. The package's version (semver, for its API) is separate from the format's (`FORMAT_VERSION`); the table below says which package versions read and write which format versions. | Package | Reads format | Writes format | |---|---|---| | 0.1.x | 1.x | 1.0 | ## Versioning The format has its own `MAJOR.MINOR` version, separate from the package's. Newer minor versions only add optional fields, which older readers ignore; a newer major version is refused with a clear message. Every older major version stays readable through an upgrader in `src/version.ts`. See [spec section 2](spec/1.0/README.md#2-versioning). ## License AGPL-3.0-or-later, the same as Gramps Connect. See [LICENSE](LICENSE). The exception is the Python writer, `python/gramps_connect_story.py`: GPL-2.0-or-later, the same as Gramps desktop, so Gramps addons can include it.
